sections.text:
David, peace be upon him, is a great prophet and king. For him, God combined prophecy and kingship in a rare precedent in the history of the children of Israel.

David's story began when he was still a young boy working in sheep herding. He was distinguished by extreme courage, physical strength, and a very sweet voice when reciting songs and praises.

At that time, the children of Israel were fighting a giant, mighty people led by a huge and terrifying king called “Goliath.”

Talut (the good king of the Children of Israel) went out with his army to fight Goliath, and on the battlefield, the giant Goliath asked for a swordsman from the army of the Children of Israel.

All the soldiers were afraid of Goliath's size and strength, but the young boy David came forward with unparalleled courage, carrying neither a sword nor a shield, but rather a slingshot (stones and rope).

David put a stone in his slingshot and aimed with extreme precision at Goliath's forehead, killing him, causing the giant to fall to death, and his army was defeated.

God Almighty said: “So they defeated them, God willing, and David killed Goliath, and God gave him dominion and wisdom.”

After this incident, the people loved David very much, and he became a great leader, then he progressed until he became their king, and God revealed to him the prophecy and revealed to him the Book of the Psalms.

God gave David amazing miracles that he had not given to anyone before him. His voice when reciting the Psalms was one of the purest and most beautiful voices ever.

When he was reciting the Psalms, the birds in the sky would stop flying to fly above him and praise God with him, and the high mountains would echo his praise in an audible voice!
Another of his miracles is that God made the iron soft in his hand for him as if it were soft dough, without the need for fire or a hammer.

David used this miracle to make unique military armor. He made “sabaghat” (wide) armor with interlocking rings, which protected the soldier and allowed him to move flexibly at the same time.

David was a just king. He judged among the people with great wisdom, and he divided his time precisely: a day for judgment, a day for worship, a day for his family, and a day for preaching to the people.

Although he was a rich king, he only ate from what he worked with his hands (from selling the armor he made), and he used to fast one day and break his fast one day, which is the best fast in the eyes of God.

One day, God tested him in his judgment to always remind him of the necessity of verifying before judging.

Two men suddenly climbed up to David's shrine (his private place of worship), and he was frightened by them. They said to him: "Do not be afraid. We are two adversaries who have fallen out and we have come to you to judge between us."

One of them said: “This is my brother. He has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe, so he became greedy about it and wanted to take it from me by force.”

David was affected by the words of the oppressed person, and he quickly judged, saying: “He has wronged you by asking your ewe to go to his ewe.”

But he immediately realized that this was a test from God, because he listened to one side and made a ruling before listening to the other side's defense!
David fell down, prostrating to God, asking for forgiveness and wept bitterly for his hasty mistake, so God forgave him, increased his sins, and improved his reputation.

David, peace be upon him, died after establishing the foundations of a strong and secure kingdom in the Holy Land, leaving his son Solomon a great legacy of wisdom and prophecy.

The lesson of David's story is the importance of justice and consistency in the judiciary, and that working by hand and earning a lawful livelihood is not incompatible with kingship and high positions.
